archetypes.name: dispatch-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan extends design-driver.sh with a new ACTION enum value and no_sentinel=true, but the plan's description of the driver's dispatch mechanism must be verified against the actual file's current code structure before implementation.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read skills/design/scripts/design-driver.sh and verify that the action whitelist syntax, sentinel mechanism, and run_action() dispatch pattern the plan describes actually exist in the current file in the form the plan expects to extend. Confirm that no_sentinel=true is an existing driver pattern rather than an invented one, that the case statement format matches the plan's proposed extension, and that VALIDATE_PLAN_COMMANDS does not collide with any existing action name. Also check whether the plan's Step 2b invocation in SKILL.md correctly mirrors the existing EMIT_PLAN invocation pattern for driver call conventions and KV output handling — a mismatch here is a wrong-target defect that the plan will silently carry into implementation. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: lint-registration
archetypes.rationale: New blocking scripts and test harnesses require registration across lint-foreground-markers.sh, Makefile test-target aggregator, and agent-lint.toml; the plan addresses these surfaces incompletely or conditionally.
archetypes.prompt_body: Check scripts/lint-foreground-markers.sh to determine whether validate-plan.sh or any other new blocking design script needs a Family B denylist entry; the plan omits this registration entirely. Verify that the Makefile changes wire both new test harnesses into the existing test-target aggregator using the exact naming convention current harness targets use — read the Makefile's current test-target pattern to confirm the proposed target names are consistent. Audit whether agent-lint.toml requires concrete exclusion entries for the new skills/design/scripts paths rather than the plan's conditional 'if exclusions are necessary' language, which defers a required decision to implementation time. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: schema-interface-completeness
archetypes.rationale: The TSV produced by parse-plan-commands.sh is the sole interface to validate-plan-commands.sh; the plan specifies both scripts independently without a complete column-level contract that can be cross-checked for producer/consumer alignment.
archetypes.prompt_body: Enumerate every TSV column name the plan implies parse-plan-commands.sh emits (block_line_start, script_path, flag columns, PARSE_NOTE rows) and every column name validate-plan-commands.sh is described as consuming, then verify the two sets are mutually consistent with no ambiguous or underdefined columns. Check whether the allowlist sidecar file format is fully specified — column names, one-row-per-entry versus one-row-per-flag shape, and whether UPDATED-script flag exemptions are encoded differently from NEW-script path exemptions — since both the parser and the validator must agree on this format without a runtime schema enforcement layer. Confirm that the KV summary keys emitted by validate-plan-commands.sh (DEFECTS_FOUND, DEFECT_COUNT, SKIPPED_COUNT) match exactly what validate-plan.sh extracts, and check whether the plan's Step 5c invocation passes a different source file (composed-plan.md) through the same pipeline in a way the parser handles without a separate code path. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
